result:
PostgreSQL assumed. Uses expand/contract: add and backfill now, drop `full_name` in a separate later migration once the app no longer reads it.

```sql
-- migrations/2026_11_24_split_full_name.sql
-- Idempotent: safe to run any number of times.

BEGIN;

-- 1. Expand: new columns (no-op if already present)
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

-- 2. Backfill only rows not yet migrated.
--    "Ada King Lovelace" -> first="Ada", last="King Lovelace"
--    "Cher"              -> first="Cher", last=NULL
--    NULL / blank        -> skipped
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_name = 'users' AND column_name = 'full_name'
  ) THEN
    UPDATE users
    SET first_name = substring(btrim(full_name) FROM '^\S+'),
        last_name  = substring(btrim(full_name) FROM '^\S+\s+(.*)$')
    WHERE first_name IS NULL
      AND last_name  IS NULL
      AND full_name IS NOT NULL
      AND btrim(full_name) <> '';
  END IF;
END $$;

COMMIT;
```

```sql
-- migrations/2026_12_xx_drop_full_name.sql
-- Contract: run only after all app code writes first_name/last_name.

BEGIN;

-- Catch rows written by old code after the backfill ran
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_name = 'users' AND column_name = 'full_name'
  ) THEN
    UPDATE users
    SET first_name = substring(btrim(full_name) FROM '^\S+'),
        last_name  = substring(btrim(full_name) FROM '^\S+\s+(.*)$')
    WHERE first_name IS NULL AND last_name IS NULL
      AND btrim(coalesce(full_name, '')) <> '';
  END IF;
END $$;

ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS full_name;

COMMIT;
```

Re-runnability: `IF NOT EXISTS`/`IF EXISTS` guard schema changes. The `WHERE first_name IS NULL AND last_name IS NULL` clause skips migrated rows, so manual edits never get overwritten. The `full_name` existence check keeps step 1 valid after the drop.

Caveats:
- Name splitting is lossy. Mononyms, "van der Berg", and family-name-first cultures won't split correctly. Show users their split name and let them fix it.
- Large tables: a single `UPDATE` holds row locks and bloats the table. Batch with `WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... LIMIT 10000)` in a loop, committing between batches. That needs a procedure or an app-side loop, not one transaction.
- Dropping too early breaks running old code. Deploy the dual-write code between the two migrations.
